reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The revelation-and-prophet report formula completes before direct lament and the how-long question begin at 1:2.
reviews.counterevidence: The heading governs the whole book and is too thin for context-free interpretation.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: How-long and why questions move through violence and strife to the doubled therefore-result in paralyzed instruction and perverted justice at 1:4.
reviews.counterevidence: Verse 1:4 has aphoristic wording and strong isolated-retrieval pressure.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: Plural look-watch-wonder imperatives open the answer, 1:6 names its instrument, and the cumulative force catalogue reaches a guilt verdict at 1:11.
reviews.counterevidence: Verse 1:6 is a strong naming turn and 1:11 shifts from description to evaluation.

challenges.claim: Verse 1:6 is a strong naming turn and 1:11 shifts from description to evaluation.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Detach 1:5, split 1:5-6 from 1:7-11, or surface catalogue fragments.
challenges.counterevidence: The naming and verdict are the opening and closing functions of one answer; internal turns remain searchable only with the complete movement.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: Renewed direct address and the why-question develop through fish, hook, net, sacrifice, prosperity, and the final mercy question; a WLC-family samekh follows 1:17.
reviews.counterevidence: The 1:12 wording is textually difficult and fish imagery turns sharply at 1:14.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: First-person stand-set-watch resolve anticipates what will be spoken; the explicit Yahweh-answered formula starts at 2:2.
reviews.counterevidence: The one-verse hinge is dependent on both neighboring movements and cannot interpret itself.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The answer formula begins write-and-wait assurance; the proud-versus-faithful contrast and insatiable gatherer lead directly to all-these at 2:6.
reviews.counterevidence: Strong internal pressures occur at 2:3|4 and 2:4|5, and the syntax and renderings in 2:4-5 remain difficult.

challenges.claim: Strong internal pressures occur at 2:3|4 and 2:4|5, and the syntax and renderings in 2:4-5 remain difficult.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Split 2:2-3, 2:4, and 2:5; include 2:1; or extend the unit through 2:6.
challenges.counterevidence: Answer continuity and the 2:5-to-2:6 antecedent outweigh semantic child seams while leaving them recorded.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The parable and taunting-proverb formula immediately voices the first woe; debtor reversal and reciprocal plunder close at 2:8 before a WLC-family pe.
reviews.counterevidence: The introduction formally governs all five woes rather than only the first.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: A new woe names evil household gain, 2:10 reverses it into shame and self-harm, and the stone-and-beam witness closes before a WLC-family pe after 2:11.
reviews.counterevidence: The building-material witness can anticipate the blood-built-city woe that opens at 2:12.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The blood-built-city woe is answered by futile labor and the earth-filling divine-purpose result; a WLC-family samekh follows 2:14.
reviews.counterevidence: Verse 2:14 has broad proverbial and canonical resonance and attracts independent retrieval.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The fourth woe opens forced drinking and exposure, 2:16 reverses the cup, and the violence-to-land-and-creatures rationale closes at 2:17 before a WLC-family samekh.
reviews.counterevidence: Verse 2:17 broadens beyond the drinking image and echoes the violence formula of 2:8.

challenges.claim: Verse 2:17 broadens beyond the drinking image and echoes the violence formula of 2:8.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Split 2:15-16 from 2:17 or detach the violence catalogue.
challenges.counterevidence: The because-clause gives the ground for the reversal, so the broadened catalogue completes rather than starts a new unit.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The 2:18 image-value question and mute-idol critique precede a samekh; a fresh woe opens at 2:19 and But Yahweh reverses mute products with living temple presence at 2:20 before a pe.
reviews.counterevidence: The samekh after 2:18 and new woe at 2:19 make the Hebrew split a substantial child-route dissent.

challenges.claim: The samekh after 2:18 and new woe at 2:19 make the Hebrew split a substantial child-route dissent.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Surface 2:18 and 2:19-20 separately, or isolate 2:20.
challenges.counterevidence: The complete idol-to-living-presence contrast is safer for retrieval, while 2:18|19 remains an explicit non-surface relation.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: The prayer and performance superscription at 3:1 governs the direct fame-work-mercy petition at 3:2; third-person advent begins at 3:3.
reviews.counterevidence: The nominal superscription and direct petition are verse-complete forms with a real 3:1|2 seam.

challenges.claim: The nominal superscription and direct petition are verse-complete forms with a real 3:1|2 seam.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Surface 3:1 and 3:2 separately or merge the petition into 3:3-7.
challenges.counterevidence: Brief title plus governed petition preserve both form and retrieval context; rare performance wording selects no setting or translation.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: God-came begins advent; glory, radiance, plague, shaking earth, crumbling mountains, and trembling tents accumulate through 3:7 before a WLC-family samekh and new river questions.
reviews.counterevidence: Selah inside 3:3 and the first-person I-saw turn at 3:7 create internal stanza pressure.

challenges.claim: Selah inside 3:3 and the first-person I-saw turn at 3:7 create internal stanza pressure.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Split at Selah inside 3:3, isolate 3:7, or retain all 3:3-15 as one surface block.
challenges.counterevidence: The samekh after 3:7 plus interrogative warrior turn at 3:8 is stronger than the internal Selah pressure.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: River-and-sea questions open at 3:8; bow, cosmic response, wrathful march, and deliverance purpose reach Selah plus pe after 3:13; second-person warrior actions continue through the horses-and-sea close at 3:15.
reviews.counterevidence: Selah, WLC-family pe, WEB line break, and the first-person object at 3:14 make 3:13|14 the strongest child-seam dissent in Habakkuk.

challenges.claim: Selah, WLC-family pe, WEB line break, and the first-person object at 3:14 make 3:13|14 the strongest child-seam dissent in Habakkuk.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Surface 3:8-13 and 3:14-15 as siblings, or isolate the salvation-purpose clause.
challenges.counterevidence: The larger unit wins narrowly because 3:14-15 complete the same march rather than initiate a new scene; the split remains explicit dissent.

reviews.support: Hebrew-textual observation: First-person bodily response returns at 3:16; the deprivation concession at 3:17 meets yet-rejoicing at 3:18 and strength, deer-foot movement, and musical subscription at 3:19.
reviews.counterevidence: The first-person return, concessive marker, emphatic response, and subscription are real internal turns.

challenges.claim: The first-person return, concessive marker, emphatic response, and subscription are real internal turns.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Evaluate the preserved alternative: Split 3:16 from 3:17-19, surface 3:17-18 alone, or detach the 3:19 confession or subscription.
challenges.counterevidence: None is safe without the embodied-response parent; the four-verse unit preserves the even-though and yet logic and performed close.
